_note: Downloaded and read the German GNI inventory in full ('ESA 2010 methods and sources for the German GNI and its components', Edition 2025, 372 pages, destatis.de) -- the same document de-destatis-national-accounts.json's _dropped array already quoted but never opened directly. Its own Chapter 10 ('Main data sources used') is a three-tier numbered table naming every source statistic by EVAS register number and title -- Research.1.md 7's strongest evidence class, applied at scale: 46 Destatis surveys (10.1), 16 other official sources mostly from the Bundesbank/BaFin/KBA (10.2), and 7 non-government sources (10.3). This slice mints the three strongest, most clearly cadenced candidates from the 46; the full table is preserved verbatim below so a future session does not have to re-download and re-parse a 4.4MB PDF to continue.
_headline: German CPI -- one of the best-known consumer price indices in the world -- was not a node in this corpus until this session, despite statcan-cpi, bls-cpi, lu-statec-ipch and eurostat-hicp all already being present.
_open_questions: Only 3 of 46 Destatis-survey rows in Chapter 10.1 are minted this session. The remaining 43, plus 16 other-official-source rows and 7 non-government rows, are transcribed verbatim below (source: Chapter 10 of the GNI inventory PDF) for a future session to work through without re-fetching the document. Candidates that stood out on a first read but were not chased: EVAS 73311/73321 (VAT/turnover-tax statistics, the single most-cited source in the whole document at 35 mentions, administrative rather than survey-based -- cadence not established this session); EVAS 47410 (the current structural survey in trade and services, successor to the now-superseded 47415); EVAS 31211 (Census of buildings and housing) and EVAS 12111 (Population census), both plausible generational-cadence nodes on the sna-2008/esa-2010 pattern but not verified live this session.

The edge direction for all three minted surveys (survey -> feeds de-destatis-national-accounts, i.e. de-destatis-national-accounts uses_data_from each survey) follows directly from Chapter 10's own table, which marks each row against the Production/Expenditure/Income approach it feeds -- this is the strongest-evidenced edge direction in the whole EU branch, a document naming its inputs in a structured table exactly as Research.1.md 7 describes it.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index for Germany
reports.description: Germany's national consumer price index, EVAS register no. 61111, listed as one of the German GNI calculation's main data sources (production, expenditure and income approaches) in the GNI inventory's own Chapter 10 table. Confirmed live on Destatis's own site: a flash/expected estimate near month-end followed by the confirmed rate roughly ten days into the following month (e.g. 'Inflation rate of +2.8% expected in July 2026' on 30 July 2026, followed by 'Inflation rate at +2.3% in June 2026' on 10 July 2026 for the prior month).
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified on destatis.de/EN/Themes/Economy/Prices/Consumer-Price-Index -- a monthly press-release series, two releases per reference month (flash estimate, then confirmed figure), same two-stage pattern already seen for eurostat-hicp.

release_schedule.note: Destatis publishes both a preliminary estimate (around the last working day of the reference month) and final results (mid-following month) for the German CPI/HICP each month. The August 12, 2026 date is directly confirmed in the July 30, 2026 press release (PD26_270_611): 'Die endgültigen Ergebnisse für Juli 2026 werden am 12. August 2026 veröffentlicht.' Subsequent dates through end of 2026 are taken from Destatis's own release calendar search tool (Terminsuche) filtered for 'verbraucherpreisindex', consistent with the standard preliminary/final monthly pattern.

reports.title: Labour Cost Survey
reports.description: EVAS register no. 62411, listed in the GNI inventory's Chapter 10 table as a production- and income-approach source. The GNI inventory's own text: 'The labour cost survey (EVAS 62411) takes place every 4 years (also 2020) and asks for the private use of car companies (benefit in kind)...' -- used among other things to allocate gross wages and salaries per employee and private use of company cars.
reports.cadence_note: Stated directly in the source document itself (the GNI inventory, p. 152 of the extracted text): 'takes place every 4 years (also 2020)'. Not independently re-verified on a separate Destatis page this session -- the GNI inventory is itself a Destatis publication and the primary source for this fact.

release_schedule.rule: The Labour Cost Survey (Arbeitskostenerhebung) is conducted every four years under EU law (Council Regulation (EC) No 530/1999 and Commission Regulation (EC) No 1737/2005) and Germany's Verdienststatistikgesetz, covering reference years 2000, 2004, 2008, ..., 2020, 2024, 2028. Eurostat's LCS metadata states 'Data for LCS2024 will be published in 2nd half of 2026,' and Destatis's April 2026 press release (PD26_148_624) states the 2024 survey results 'werden voraussichtlich im Juli 2026 veröffentlicht' (are expected to be published in July 2026).
release_schedule.note: As of the research date (2026-08-11), no press release or dataset confirming the actual July 2026 publication of AKE2024 detailed results could be located via search — the target month has just passed and the release may have slipped slightly (Destatis used 'voraussichtlich' = 'expected'). The prior cycle (LCS2020) was published July 2022 (PD22_280_624), i.e. about 2 years after the reference year, consistent with the 2024→2026 pattern. If AKE2024 has already been published by the time this is read, the next occurrence would instead be AKE2028, expected to be published in the second half of 2030.

reports.title: Quarterly Production Survey in Manufacturing, Mining and Quarrying
reports.description: EVAS register no. 42131, listed in the GNI inventory's Chapter 10 table as a production- and expenditure-approach source, one of a family of items surveys covering manufacturing/mining/quarrying (alongside the cost structure survey, EVAS 42251, and the investment survey, EVAS 42231). Named directly in Chapter 6's discussion of output calculation: 'Production statistics by products and industries (EVAS 42131)'. CORRECTION 2026-08-09 (EU/G.74.md): domains was ['manufacturing'], which is not a member of the Domain union and never has been — the sole such value corpus-wide, undetected because nothing outside types.ts reads the field. Retagged 'national-accounts', which is the corpus's own convention for a production or manufacturing survey feeding the accounts (statcan-msm, statcan-asml, nl-cbs-sbs, au-abs-australian-industry all carry it) and is what this record's own description says it is — a GNI-inventory production- and expenditure-approach source. No new Domain member was minted: one node is not evidence that the union is missing a category, and 'manufacturing' as used here is the survey's subject matter rather than an economic domain in this field's sense. Nothing about the survey itself is corrected; the original description above is unchanged.
reports.cadence_note: Cadence stated in the survey's own title as given in the GNI inventory's Chapter 10 table ('Quarterly production survey'); not independently re-verified on a separate Destatis genesis-online page this session.

release_schedule.rule: Quartalsergebnisse werden innerhalb von dreieinhalb Monaten nach Abschluss des Berichtsquartals veröffentlicht. (Quarterly results [of the Vierteljährliche Produktionserhebung, EVAS 42131] are published within three and a half months after the end of the reporting quarter.) Reporting deadline for respondents is no later than 12 days after the end of the reference quarter.
release_schedule.note: This is the official coordinated federal/Länder metadata report (EVAS 42121/42131) for the 'Monatliche und Vierteljährliche Produktionserhebung im Bereich Verarbeitendes Gewerbe, Bergbau und Gewinnung von Steinen und Erden' survey, which is the German-language name for the report in question (EVAS 42131 = the quarterly survey). Q1 2026 results (ending 2026-03-31) would have been due by roughly 2026-07-15, which has already passed relative to today (2026-08-11); the next unreleased quarter is Q2 2026, due by roughly 2026-10-15. Note the standalone print publication 'Fachserie 4 Reihe 3.1' (dated PDF editions) was discontinued after the Q4/full-year 2018 edition ('Diese Publikation wird letztmalig mit der Jahresausgabe 2018 veröffentlicht'), but the underlying survey/data series (EVAS 42131, GENESIS-Online table 42131) continues on the stated quarterly schedule; results now appear only via GENESIS-Online tables rather than a dated PDF report, so no dated 'published-calendar' entries could be found, only the stated timeliness rule.
